title: Workshop on “Transmission Assessment” Held by the Department
text:
The Department recently organized a workshop titled “Transmission Assessment” with the participation of staff members across the unit. The session focused on providing foundational knowledge and methodologies for evaluating the transmissibility of infectious diseases to support surveillance and outbreak response.
The workshop introduced key concepts such as the reproduction number (R), generation time, and other indicators used to analyze disease transmission dynamics. The reporting team also presented methods for estimating time-varying R, analyzing epidemiological trends, and interpreting results to inform decision-making.



Team members getting ready for the presentation.


Participants engaged in active discussions on the applicability of each method in real-world settings, including assessing outbreak risk, forecasting epidemic trends, and supporting resource prioritization during response activities.
The workshop concluded with a shared direction to strengthen the use of transmission-assessment methods in routine surveillance, contributing to improved forecasting capacity and more effective disease control.

title: Workshop on Collaboration with OUCRU for Rt Research in Dengue
text:
The Department of Surveillance, Warning, Preparedness, and Emergency Response recently held a workshop to present the research concept on the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) in Dengue with representatives from OUCRU.
During the session, the department introduced its proposed study on estimating Rt and its potential application in disease surveillance. Both sides discussed initial steps for collaboration, including research design, data sharing, and strengthening analytical capacity in epidemiology.

title: Phân tích dữ liệu với R
text:
R project

Tạo Project trong R Studio
R project là một thư mục với file .Rproj . Để thuận tiện cho việc quản lý code và dữ liệu, ta nên tạo R project cho mỗi nghiên cứu/ báo cáo.
Quá trình tạo R project như sau:

Vào menu File > New Project
Bấm New Directory > New Project
Điền tên folder cho R Project tại mục Directory name
Bấm Browse và chọn Desktop để lưu R project tại Desktop
Bấm Create Project



Cấu trúc của một Project
Cấu trúc của một R project sẽ có định dạng như sau:


data thư mục chứa dữ liệu cần phân tích
output lưu trữ đầu ra mã (cốt truyện, số liệu, v.v.)
analysis.R là tệp chứa mã R. Có thể có nhiều file .R trong 1 project.



R markdown
File .Rmd thường được dùng cho báo cáo vì có thể kết hợp các lệnh R, văn bản thường, đồ thị trong 1 file 
Gồm 3 phần chính:

Phần YAML header: nằm ở trên cùng trong và ngăn cách với phần còn lại bằng cặp dấu ---. Phần này để mô tả tiêu đề tài liệu, tác giả, ngày tháng, định dạng mong muốn
Phần văn bản (được viết bằng ngôn ngữ markdown)
Phần lệnh R (được gọi là chunk). Phần kết quả của câu lệnh R (chunk output) có thể hiển thị dưới dạng string, bảng dữ liệu hoặc đồ thị.


Tạo R Markdown bằng cách vào menu File > New File > R Markdown...

title: SWAPER
text:
Our mission
The Department of Surveillance, Warning, Preparedness, and Emergency Response is tasked with protecting public health through a structured and systematic approach. The department’s mandate is executed through three primary missions:
1. To Ensure the Quality of the Public Health Monitoring System
This mission focuses on the development and oversight of processes that guarantee the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of data from all public health surveillance systems. It includes conducting systematic evaluations and rapid surveys to inform and continuously improve monitoring strategies.
2. To Monitor, Detect, and Alert on Unusual Health Events
This mission involves the systematic collection and management of epidemiological data to monitor health trends, forecast outcomes, and assess risks. The objective is to promptly detect unusual events, issue evidence-based alerts, and propose scientifically grounded solutions to mitigate public health threats.
3. To Prepare for and Respond to Public Health Emergencies
This mission centers on maintaining a high state of operational readiness. It includes managing the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (PHEOC) and the Provincial Rapid Response Teams (RRT), and implementing comprehensive preparedness activities such as planning, training, drills, and resource allocation for effective emergency response.

title: SWAPER
text:
Our work
To accomplish these missions, the department is organized into two primary divisions with distinct functions:
Division of Surveillance and Warning
This division is responsible for all data collection, analysis, and risk assessment functions. Its key responsibilities include:

Assessing the performance and quality of existing surveillance systems.
Developing and implementing an integrated, digital disease surveillance system, including an early warning mechanism for schools and communities, with a target for completion by 2025.
Conducting formal risk assessments for endemic, zoonotic, and emerging/re-emerging infectious diseases.
Establishing official epidemic warning thresholds for all administrative levels (city and ward).
Developing and applying mathematical models for the purpose of forecasting disease outbreaks.
Defining and utilizing key data indicators for the evaluation of outbreak severity and response effectiveness.

Division of Preparedness and Emergency Response
This division is responsible for all operational planning, readiness, and response coordination. Its key responsibilities include:

Advising on and developing the legal and operational frameworks for the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (PHEOC) and the Rapid Response Teams (RRT).
Developing and standardizing operational guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the PHEOC and RRTs.
Creating and managing the activation system for the Rapid Response Teams.
Overseeing the strategic planning, procurement, and maintenance of essential infrastructure, equipment, and supplies for emergency response.
Providing technical guidance on the development of the city’s long-term Pandemic Response Plan for 2030 and beyond.

title: SWAPER
text:
Collaboration
We maintain strong working relationships with leading academic research institutions, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and other specialized departments within the Ho Chi Minh City Center for Disease Control (HCDC).
These partnerships are vital for conducting cutting-edge research, validating new methodologies, and strengthening the city’s overall public health framework. Notable partners include the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit (OUCRU) and FHI 360.
A selection of key research projects undertaken through these collaborations includes:

Evaluation of the Reproduction Number (Rt) in Measles Outbreaks in HCMC.
Methods for Determining Epidemic Thresholds in Endemic Disease Surveillance: A Scoping Review and Benchmark.
Dengue Advanced Readiness Tools (DART).
Assessment of the Infectious Disease and Public Health Event Surveillance System in HCMC.
A Review of Methodological Approaches to Infectious Disease Risk Assessment.
Event-Based Surveillance Using Social Media, Google Search Data, and Online News Media.

text:
Package ggplot2

ggplot2 hoạt động trực tiếp với dữ liệu tidy (giống như mọi thứ trong tidyverse).
Nó dựa trên một khái niệm gọi là grammar of graphics.
Có tài liệu hướng dẫn toàn diện về cách sử dụng.
Cung cấp đủ tính linh hoạt để tùy chỉnh.

title: Trực quan hóa dữ liệu với R
text:
Cấu trúc của ggplot2

Một khuôn khổ để mô tả và xây dựng biểu đồ theo cách có cấu trúc.
Phương pháp tiếp cận theo layer, tức là mỗi thành phần của một hình là các layer riêng biệt.



Ví dụ

Hãy xem code ví dụ sau:


ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  scale_x_continuous("Weight (1000 lbs)") +
  scale_y_continuous("Miles Per Gallon") +
  ggtitle("MPG vs. Weight") + 
  theme_bw()









Data: mtcars
Aesthetics: aes(x = wt, y = mpg)
Geometries: geom_point
Coordinates: scale_x_continuous, scale_y_continuous
Theme: theme_bw, ggtitle







Tip



ggplot2 chỉ chạy với dữ liệu là data frame và không thể chạy với loại dữ liệu khác (ví dụ: ma trận hoặc vectơ).




Aesthetics

Phải đặt trong aes().
Khai báo thông tin các trục x, y.
Khai báo màu sắc color, fill.


df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:10,
  y = (1:10)^2,
  group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5)
) 




ggplot(df, aes(x, y, color = group)) + 
  geom_col()










ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = group)) + 
  geom_col()












Geometries

geom_col or geom_bar: biểu đồ cột/ thanh
geom_histogram: histograms
geom_point: biểu đồ chấm (scatter)
geom_line or geom_smooth: biểu đồ đường (làm mượt)
geom_boxplot: biểu đồ hộp







Tip



Data, aesthetic, geometric đối tượng là thành phần quan trọng của biểu đồ, nếu cấu trúc này không đủ thì cốt truyện sẽ không hoạt động.




Shape of geom_point



Coordinates

Tùy chỉnh hiển thị của các trục: scale_x_..., scale_y_..., xlim, ylim,…
Tùy chỉnh màu sắc theo giá trị của từng biến: scale_color_..., scale_fill_...,…
Tùy chỉnh tên cột, tên biểu đồ, tên chú thích: labs



Themes

Tùy chỉnh background của biểu đồ: màu sắc, lưới,…
Tùy chỉnh kiểu chữ trên biểu đồ.
Có sẵn một số theme để lựa chọn: theme_classic, theme_minimal,…

title: Meeting with OUCRU
text:
On July 02, 2025, the SWAPER development team held a formal meeting with representatives from the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit (OUCRU) in Ho Chi Minh City. This was one of the initial steps in building a long-term partnership between the two organizations, centered around infectious disease surveillance and applied epidemiological research.
The meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to discuss key challenges in early warning systems, explore local data collection needs at the district level, and share perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence in outbreak detection and prediction. OUCRU shared their experience with previous research projects, while SWAPER presented their ongoing efforts to digitize surveillance workflows and develop integrated platforms for real-time monitoring.
The atmosphere of the meeting was open and collaborative, fostering mutual understanding and laying the groundwork for future joint initiatives. As of July 2025, the discussions from this meeting have helped shape several shared projects and contributed to a growing network of partners committed to improving public health systems in Vietnam.

This was one of the initial steps in building a long-term partnership between the two organizations, centered around infectious disease surveillance and applied epidemiological research.
The meeting provided an opportunity for both sides to discuss key challenges in early warning systems, explore local data collection needs at the district level, and share perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence in outbreak detection and prediction. OUCRU shared their experience with previous research projects, while SWAPER presented their ongoing efforts to digitize surveillance workflows and develop integrated platforms for real-time monitoring.
The atmosphere of the meeting was open and collaborative, fostering mutual understanding and laying the groundwork for future joint initiatives. As of July 2025, the discussions from this meeting have helped shape several shared projects and contributed to a growing network of partners committed to improving public health systems in Vietnam.

title: Workshop on the Chikungunya Situation in France and Italy
text:
The Department of Surveillance, Warning, Preparedness, and Emergency Response organized an internal workshop to update team members on the current Chikungunya situation in France and Italy, where an increase in reported cases has recently been observed.
During the session, participants reviewed epidemiological trends in both countries and discussed the key factors contributing to the rise in cases, including the expanding distribution of Aedes albopictus, the impact of climate change creating favorable conditions for vector breeding, and high volumes of international travel during the summer season.
This activity strengthened the team’s understanding of Chikungunya transmission risks and supported the department’s early warning efforts.

title: Workshop Spatial Analysis and Risk map
text:
Recently, the Department organized a workshop on “Spatial Analysis” with the participation of members from the Surveillance and Early Warning Division (GSCB). The session provided foundational knowledge on spatial analysis, the development of dengue risk maps, and various approaches for applying spatial modeling in epidemiology.
During the workshop, participants were introduced to an overview of key spatial analysis techniques and global examples of risk-mapping approaches. These insights helped identify lessons learned and inform directions for developing a risk map tailored to the context of Ho Chi Minh City. Members also engaged in active discussions on data application, spatial modeling, and practical implementation for dengue.
The department organized a workshop to introduce Risk Map, a tool that supports visualization, management, and prediction of infectious disease risks based on case data. The tool displays spatial risk distribution, helping identify priority areas for investigation and informing decision-making in surveillance and outbreak response activities.
Risk Map integrates multiple data sources, including case data, population density, growth patterns, and other transmission-related factors. It visualizes risk levels through graded color scales, incorporates hotspots and the growthRate indicator for early warning, and supports prioritization of resources such as vaccines and healthcare personnel.
The workshop provided an overview of Risk Map’s potential applications in analysis and decision support, contributing to improved effectiveness in disease prevention and control.

title: Workshop on Using the EIOS System for Monitoring Public Health Events
text:
The Department of Surveillance, Warning, Preparedness, and Emergency Response organized an internal workshop on the Epidemic Intelligence from Open Sources (EIOS) system to strengthen the team’s capacity in early detection of public health events.
During the session, members were introduced to how EIOS collects, aggregates, and filters information from various open sources, including news outlets, social media, and online platforms. The workshop also focused on how to use EIOS to identify unusual signals, monitor disease trends, and support early warning activities.
